summary.headline: Indo Count guides FY27 revenue to about INR5,500 crore (over 30% growth) and EBITDA margin to about 13%, versus 11% in FY26.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue was flat at about INR4,211 crore (total income) versus INR4,191 crore in FY25, but EBITDA fell to INR461 crore (11% margin) from INR577 crore (13.8%) on new-business incubation costs, lower fixed-cost absorption and case-by-case tariff sharing. Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR1,088 crore (QoQ from INR1,074 crore), with EBITDA of INR116 crore (10.7% margin) and PAT of INR24 crore. Core business fell by a low-teens percentage in FY26 on U.S. tariff volatility, while new business revenue reached INR792 crore. Management guided FY27 to a record year with volumes of 105-110 million meters (FY26: 94 million) and consolidated revenue of about INR5,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: INR792 crore (about USD270 million per the call's INR270 crore figure for the quarter)

segments.name: Core business
segments.commentary: Core business declined by a low-teens percentage in FY26 due to U.S. tariffs; non-U.S. share was about 30% of core revenue, with FY27 non-U.S. growth guided at 20%. Core FY27 revenue guided at about INR4,000 crore, with core EBITDA margin targeted at about 15%.

segments.name: New business (utility bedding and U.S. brands)
segments.commentary: New business revenue was INR792 crore in FY26, split about 2/3 utility bedding and 1/3 brands, and is guided to about INR1,500 crore in FY27. Management said new business is now EBITDA positive, with utility bedding targeted at 15% margin and brands at 100-200 bps above core margin.

segments.name: U.S. utility bedding
segments.commentary: Three U.S. facilities now produce 31 million pillows and 1.5 million quilts per year (up from 13 million pillows). The two older facilities run at about 65% utilisation, with 60-65% across all three targeted in FY27; management said this level is EBITDA positive.

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Domestic business under brands Boutique Clothing and Layers contributed about 2.25% of FY26 revenue, with about 2,000 touch points.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of about INR5,500 crore, growth of over 30%; incremental revenue of about INR1,300 crore, of which core about INR4,000 crore and new business about INR1,500 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of around 13%, including other income; management said core business is kept at about 15% in this guidance.
FY27 volume guidance of 105-110 million meters versus 94.1 million meters in FY26.
Non-U.S. core revenue expected to grow 20% in FY27.
Target of about USD275 million (about INR2,500 crore) in new business by 2028 and revenue doubling by 2028 over the FY25 base (about INR8,000 crore run rate, stated as sometime in calendar 2028).
Capex outlay of INR250 crore over the next 12-18 months, funded 75% internal accruals and 25% debt; long-term debt repayment of about INR85-90 crore a year for the next couple of years.
Tax rate of 25%; no change expected in interest profile or effective tax rate.
Company expects to pass on raw material cost increases to customers within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: U.S. utility bedding: North Carolina greenfield facility commenced operations in FY26, taking U.S. facilities to three with capacity of 31 million pillows and 1.5 million quilts per year (from 13 million pillows).
Existing two U.S. utility bedding facilities at about 65% utilisation; overall 60-65% utilisation across three facilities targeted in FY27.
Planned capex of INR250 crore over 12-18 months, to be funded by internal accruals and debt; management said the company has largely completed its planned growth investments.
Cotton sourcing: about 70% domestic and 30% imported (Egyptian and American extra-long staple); import share expected to stay around 30%.
demand_pricing: No customer loss or order cancellations in FY26, per management; some tariff impact was absorbed to protect share.

Orders are placed about 60 days ahead; customers planned around 50% U.S. tariff until mid-February 2026, when it reduced to 10%, causing Q4 volume weakness (20.5 million meters vs about 24-25 million in earlier quarters).
U.S. retailers have raised retail prices and consumers have accepted them; management said there is no restocking and sales flow is at normalised levels.
Q4 realisations rose on forex gains and a more favourable product mix; management said product mix is normalising after prior down-trading.

Raw material cost inflation (cotton, yarn, polyester, dyes, chemicals, energy, packaging) over the last 30-60 days; repricing with customers is in progress. Indian cotton import duty waiver notified recently, which management said levels the playing field for Indian sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and debt evolve over the next four quarters given tariff relief, a weaker INR and higher cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 13% margin guidance, citing recent raw material inflation that will be passed on through repricing. Long-term debt repayment is INR85-90 crore a year; the INR250 crore capex is 75% internally funded and 25% debt-funded.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 revenue guidance backed by visibility, and why does new business double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is at about INR1,100 crore run rate, with Q4 new business at about INR270 crore; it cited business visibility, with no specific pipeline numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Will utility bedding reach EBITDA breakeven, and when will the greenfield facility do so?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer reports by facility. At 60-65% utilisation on 31 million pillows, the segment is EBITDA positive; the 150-200 bps launch drag ends from Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin guide only 13% when the company historically earned 15-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Core business is kept at about 15% in guidance; new business was previously a drag but is now EBITDA positive, so it is expected to add to margins gradually. Management declined to comment on Q4 FY27 margin exit rate.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 doubling-of-revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed the target of about INR8,000 crore run rate by 2028 (calendar year), not within FY27-28, and declined to give more detail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effect of the Indian cotton import duty waiver, and what will the import mix be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30% of raw material is imported (long/extra-long staple, exempt from duty already); the waiver levels the field for domestic cotton, and the import share is expected to stay near 30%.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (cotton, polyester, energy, packaging) and the speed of repricing with U.S. customers; management said a lag effect is possible.
Dependence on U.S. tariff levels: the 50% tariff through mid-February 2026 drove Q4 volumes down; future tariff or trade-deal changes could shift demand.
Utility bedding and brand ramp-up: utilisation must reach 60-65% across three U.S. facilities for the EBITDA-positive claim; Wamsutta revenue is still small and undisclosed.
Other income (about INR30 crore in Q4) is largely forex-driven and may not be sustained, per the call's own discussion.

Working capital: management said incremental revenue would come at about 120 days working capital, so the FY27 revenue jump requires substantial funding; floating-rate debt exposed to interest rate changes.
Management declined to comment on quarterly trajectory (Q1 FY27 versus Q4) and on the Q4 FY27 margin exit rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story and the FY27 record-year guidance, but cautious and terse on specifics: management declined to give facility-level data, quarterly guidance, or the Q4 FY27 margin exit rate, and repeatedly stated the FY28 target as a run rate for calendar 2028 rather than a fiscal-year target.

I think it will remain at 30%. We don't see any much big change.
